questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

Seeing a rainbow (1)/ is a sight (2)/ to behold. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: The given sentence contains no error as it simply tells that seeing a rainbow is a glimpse worthy of seeing. Therefore, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

The poor girl slept in the attic, upon a hard straw mattress, (1)/ whilst the bed-chambers of the sisters (2)/ were furnishing with every luxury and elegance. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: Solution: The sentence is in past tense as suggested by ‘slept’ and ‘were’. Therefore, the verb furnish should be in the past tense too. Hence, ‘furnished’ should be written instead of ‘furnishing’. The error is therefore in part 3 of the sentence and option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**The sentence(s) given with blanks are to be filled with an appropriate word(s). Four alternatives are suggested for each question. For each question, choose the correct alternative and click the button corresponding to it.**

My family has always ______ me.
questions.solution: The usage of ‘has’ in the given sentence that the action that started in the past still continues in the present. Therefore, the present perfect tense (**sub + has/have + v3 + object** ) should be used. So the main verb supported should be in its third form, i.e., ‘supported’.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent sentence.**

The country

P: due to the

Q: new Prime Minister

R: is in dire straits
questions.solution: R mentions the state in which the country is. P and Q combine to state the reason. Therefore, RPQ is the correct sequence. Note that the state of a particular thing should come before you mention the reason behind it.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent sentence.**

There is

P: gap between

Q: a huge financial

R: the two families
questions.solution: R should definitely follow P as between indicates that there must be two entities. Q has to be the first part as it states what kind of gap is there. Thus, QPR is the correct sequence.

questions.question: Inhabitants of the Earth have cleared ________ forests to make fields for growing crops.
questions.solution: ‘To clear away’ is a phrasal verb which means to ‘remove’, ‘exhaust’ or ‘finish’. Thus, ‘away’ is the correct adverb that should be used here as the forests have been removed to grow crops.

questions.question: They have moved mountains to make ________ for roads
questions.solution: The phrase ‘to make room’ means to remove things to make space for another. In the given context it means that mountains have been cut through to make roads and cities.

questions.question: They have built huge dams ________ rivers
questions.solution: You build dams ‘across’ rivers, that is, they are built from one side to another. Thus option 3 is correct.

questions.question: Once everyone cheered at the progress that man made in changing his _________
questions.solution: From all the progress mentioned earlier in the passage, it can be understood that man made changes in his surrounding or the *environment*. Option 2 is quite a broad term and man may not make changes in it completely. ‘Ecology’ is a branch of study, and is an unfit for the given blank. Option 3 is inappropriate too.

questions.question: many people are worried by the ___________ that such changes can bring.
questions.solution: One cannot be worried about ‘advantages’, ‘benefits’ or ‘agreements’. ‘Problems’ are something to be worried about, therefore, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
If 9 @ 3 @ 2 = 28 and 11 @ 2 @ 1 = 28, then

5 @ 4 @ 5 = ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

9 @ 3 @ 2 → (9 + 3 + 2) × 2 = 28

11 @ 2 @ 1 → (11 + 2 + 1) × 2 = 28

Similarly,

5 @ 4 @ 5 → (5 + 4 + 5) × 2 = 28

Hence, the answer is 28.

questions.question: Rohit scored 44, 42, 62, 74, 40, and 26 runs in a six-match one-day cricket series. What is his average score for the series?
questions.solution:
⇒ Total runs scored by Rohit = 44 + 42 + 62 + 74 + 40 + 26

⇒ Total runs scored by Rohit = 288

⇒ Average score for the series = Total runs scored/Number of innings

⇒ Average score for the series = 288/6

∴ Average score for the series = 48

questions.question: A shopkeeper offers 13% discount on a car tyre with a marked price of Rs. 8800. If he still earns a profit of Rs. 1200, what is the cost price of the tyre?
questions.solution:
⇒ Marked price of Car tyre = Rs. 8800

⇒ Discount = 13% of 8800 = Rs. 1144

⇒ SP = MP – Discount

⇒ Selling Price = 8800 – 1144

⇒ Selling Price = Rs. 7656

⇒ Profit = Rs. 1200(given)

⇒ Cost Price = Selling Price – Profit

⇒ Cost Price = 7656 - 1200

∴ Cost Price = Rs. 6456

questions.question: The sum of all even whole numbers between 13 and 43 is ____.
questions.solution:
⇒ required sum = 14 + 16 + 18 + ……… + 42

⇒ This is in A.P in which a = 14, d = 2, l = 42

⇒ Let the number of terms in it be n

⇒ a + (n – 1) d = 42

⇒ 14 + (n – 1) ⨯ 2 = 42

⇒ 14 + 2n - 2 = 42

⇒ n = 15

∴ required sum = n/2 (a + l) = 15/2 (14 + 42) = 7.5 ⨯ 56 = 420

∴ x = Rs. 30000

questions.question: Manoj does a work in 20 days and Sahil does the same work in 30 days. In how many days they together will do the same work?
questions.solution:
⇒ Manoj can do a piece of work in 20 days

⇒ Manoj’s 1 day work = 1/20

⇒ Sahil can do a piece of work in 30 days

⇒ Sahil’s 1 day work = 1/30

⇒ Now Manoj and Sahil’s 1 day work = 1/20 + 1/30

⇒ Manoj and Sahil’s 1 day work = (3 + 2)/60 = 5/60 = 1/12

∴ Manoj and Sahil together can do in 12 days

questions.question: A number when divided by 6 leaves a remainder 4. When the square of the number is divided by 6 the remainder is ____.
questions.solution:
⇒ Let x = 6q + 4

⇒ x² = (6q + 4)²

⇒ x² = (36q² + 16 + 48q)

⇒ x² = 6(6q² + 12 + 8q) + 4

∴ When x² is divided by 6, then remainder = 4

questions.question: What is the unit’s digit in the product (813 × 986 × 471 × 603)?

⇒ Unit digit in the product (813 × 986 × 471 × 603) = Unit digit in the product (3 × 6 × 1 × 3) = 54

∴ Unit digit in the product (813 × 986 × 471 × 603) = 4

questions.question: The monthly salaries of A and B are in the ratio 9 : 10. If both of them get a salary increment of Rs. 6000 per month, the new ratio becomes 21 : 23. What is the new monthly salary of A?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The monthly salaries of A and B are in the ratio 9 : 10. If both of them get a salary increment of Rs. 6000 per month, the new ratio becomes 21 : 23

**Calculation:**

Let the monthly salaries of A and B be 9a and 10a respectively.

Both get increment of Rs. 6000 per month = (9a + 6000)/(10a + 6000)

After increment, new ratio is 21 : 23

solving (9a + 6000)/(10a + 6000) = 21/23

We get, a = 4000

The new monthly salary of A = (9 × 4000 + 6000) = Rs. 42000

**∴ the correct answer is Rs.42000.**

questions.question: The sum of 10 consecutive integers is 5. What is the lowest integer?
questions.solution:
⇒ lets denote the smallest of 10 consecutive integers as N

⇒ N + (N + 1) + (N + 2) + …. + (N + 9) = 5

⇒ 10N + 45 = 5

⇒ N = -4

∴ The lowest integer is -4

questions.question: A cyclist covers a distance of 8 kms in 30 minutes. What is his average speed?
questions.solution:
⇒ Distance = 8 kms

⇒ Time = 30 minutes = ½ hour

⇒ Average speed = Total Distance/Total time

⇒ Average speed = 8/(1/2) km/hr

∴ Average speed = 16 km/hr

questions.question: Manjeet's annual salary was reduced by 30% and subsequent year increased by 45%. What is the overall percentage change over his original salary?
questions.solution:
⇒ Let Manjeet salary be 100a

⇒ After reduction of 30%, salary becomes (70/100) x 100a = 70a

⇒ Next year salary increased by 45%, new salary = (145/100) x 70a = 101.5a

⇒ The overall change over his original salary = 101.5a – 100a = 1.5a

⇒ Overall percentage change = (change in salary /original salary) x 100

∴ Change in % = (1.5a/100a)/100 = 1.5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Let the present annual salary be 100

⇒ After a reduction of 30%, salary becomes,

70/100 × 100 = 70

⇒ Next year salary increased by 45%, new salary = 145/100 × 70 = 101.5

Thus, Overall percentage change = 1.5/100 × 100 = **1.5%**

questions.question: A fruit vendor buys 5 dozen bananas for Rs. 240. What should be the price per pair of the banana so that the vendor can earn 25% profit?
questions.solution:
⇒ Cost of 5 dozen bananas = Rs. 240

⇒ Profit = 25%

⇒ Selling Price = 240 + 25% of 240 = Rs. 300

⇒ Selling price of 60 bananas = Rs. 300

⇒ Selling price of pair of bananas = (300/60) × 2

⇒ Selling price of pair of bananas = 5 × 2

∴ Selling price of pair of bananas = Rs. 10

questions.question: Rakesh can do a piece of work in 20 hours. After he works at it for 8 hours, how much part of the work would be left?
questions.solution:
⇒ Time taken to complete the work by Rakesh = 20 hours

⇒ Rakesh’s 1 hour work = 1/20

⇒ Work done by Rakesh in 8 hours = 8/20 = 2/5

⇒ Part of work left after 8 hours = 1 – (2/5)

∴ Part of work left after 8 hours = 3/5

questions.question: How many whole numbers are there between 48 and 352 which are exactly divisible by 7?
questions.solution:
⇒ Required number = 49, 56, 63, 70, ………, 350

⇒ This is in A.P in which a = 49, d = 7 and l = 350

⇒ Let the number of terms in it be n

⇒ l = a + (n – 1) d

⇒ 350 = 49 + (n – 1) ⨯ 7

⇒ 350 = 49 + 7n – 7

⇒ 7n = 350 – 42

⇒ 7n = 308

∴ n = 44
